description: Solo game developer, narrative designer, and 3D environment builder operating under Something in Gaming. Focusing on 3D world-building, interactive storytelling, and immersive design to build an engaging Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for the Erode local event. Working solo for this challenge!
summary: Lunar  Outpost  is an interactive 3D space-themed STEM hybrid game where players command a crew of six specialists inside a pressurized Lunar Bio-Dome and experience first-hand how real aerospace engineering trade-offs determine whether a moon mission fails or succeeds. Combining real-time resource allocation across four competing outpost demands—Life Support, Radiation Shielding, Power, and Food Production—with dynamic dome radius expansion, In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) regolith mining, hydroponic farming, stealth, and alien defense, the simulation trains junior astronauts in authentic lunar habitat survival. Every power or shielding decision directly impacts crew safety, crop growth, and mission survival until escape rocket liftoff.
details:
Lunar Outpost is an interactive 3D lunar habitat survival and STEM engineering simulation set on a cratered Moon landscape. Players command six autonomous crew specialists inside a pressurized glass bio-dome without spacesuits. Because stepping outside the dome's protective barrier is lethal, players must dynamically expand or shrink the dome's radius using power and magnetic radiation shielding—expanding outward to safely enclose outdoor In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) machinery (Lunar Regolith Digger, Dual-Turbine Power Station, and Dual-Ring Radiation Station) and shrinking inward during Solar Storms while relying on a central Fusion Core to maintain a minimum safe threshold.

4-Genre Hybrid Mechanics:

  1. Engineering Trade-Off Strategy: Players divide a 100-point power budget across four live survival bars—Life Support (O2), Radiation Shielding, Power, and Food Production—where letting any bar reach 0% causes mission failure.
  2. ISRU Mining & Hydroponic Farming: Operating the Lunar Digger extracts Water Ice and Helium-3 to fuel the Power Station and irrigate indoor hydroponic beds growing NASA space lettuce and bioluminescent alien mushrooms for hybrid lab research.
  3. Stealth & Tactical Defense: Players use crouch mechanics, flashlight management, and physical cover to evade scanner cones during power blackouts while defending the outpost against mutating alien organisms until completing research and launching the escape rocket.

Benefits, Creativity & Factors Considered: Rather than teaching spaceflight concepts passively, the simulation lets junior astronauts experience how real aerospace engineering trade-offs cascade across life support, energy, radiation protection, and food systems. Key design factors included authentic NASA Artemis ISRU resource chains, closed-loop botanical O2 regeneration, and intuitive 3D visual feedback (dynamic dome scaling and live visor telemetry).

Tools, Hardware, Coding Languages & SI Disclosure: Built using TypeScript, Three.js / WebGL, Blender (for 3D modeling, rigging, and asset optimization), and Jabali AI Studio on a Windows PC workstation. Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment: Jabali AI and Google Gemini were utilized to assist with TypeScript/Three.js code generation, descriptive documentation, and the in-game BALI holographic assistant dialogue. All core game mechanics, engineering trade-off systems, 3D model rigging, and level architecture were designed and assembled by our team.
